ai.title: Add gpt-4.1 model and --model CLI param support
ai.summary: Added `gpt-4.1` to OpenAI model constants, cost tracking, and message transformation logic. Introduced `prompt-agent-stream.ts` to centralize model selection based on `selectedModel` param or cost mode, replacing direct provider calls in `main-prompt.ts`. Updated `websocket-action.ts` and `actions.ts` schema to pass `model` string from client. Added specific instruction suppression for `gpt-4.1` in `main-prompt.ts` to handle its reasoning behavior.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant to use OpenAI's newer gpt-4.1 model when you run it, and you can pick that model from the command line instead of relying on the default automatic choice. The assistant will figure out which model to talk to (OpenAI's gpt-4.1, the usual GPT-4o/O-mini set, or Anthropic's Claude) based on what you specify or the cost mode, and it tracks the price of using gpt-4.1 just like the other models. If you look, you'd see a new option named --model you can pass in, and when gpt-4.1 is selected it quietly skips a reasoning hint that doesn't help that particular model.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.216
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.216 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: When you update to the latest version of your AI coding assistant, it can now use a newer model that understands requests more accurately. You'll also be able to pick which model the assistant uses through a new command-line option, and referrals now earn double the previous credit reward. The update also delivers several behind-the-scenes reliability fixes to background processing and prompt handling.

ai.title: Replace lastUserPromptIndex with consecutiveAssistantMessages counter
ai.summary: Refactored agent state tracking in `common/src/types/agent-state.ts` and `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Replaced `lastUserPromptIndex` with a `consecutiveAssistantMessages` counter to simplify logic for detecting excessive assistant turns. Initial state now defaults to 0 instead of -1. The warning trigger and `end_turn` tool call remain functionally identical.

eli5.text: When the AI keeps answering in a row without you chipping in, it will now notice that sooner and pause to check if you still want it to go on. The system previously tried to remember where your last message was to count the gap; it now just keeps a running tally of how many times in a row it spoke, which makes the same check simpler and starts the count at zero instead of -1. You won't see this directly unless the AI was about to ramble too long, at which point you'd notice it stopping earlier with the same message it always used. This tweak is live now and only changes when, not whether, that pause happens.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.217
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.217 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: If you use the coding assistant, updating to this version lets the assistant now work with OpenAI's newer gpt-4.1 model through either a command-line option or an automatic setting. The assistant will also keep track of its own replies instead of counting your prompts when deciding how to respond. This update went live on April 14, 2025. If you're an internal user or administrator, you might notice the assistant behaves slightly more reliably across multiple turns, especially when using the new model selection.

ai.title: Throw server error on invalid model in getAgentStream
ai.summary: Added validation in `getAgentStream` to throw an error if `selectedModel` is not a key in `shortModelNames`. This prevents downstream failures when an invalid model string is passed to the backend stream handler. The change applies to `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`. The error message lists valid models via `Object.keys(shortModelNames).join(', ')`.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to use a model name that doesn't exist, the system will now immediately tell you which model names are valid instead of failing silently later. This only affects the internal assistant backend, so it doesn't change anything you see in the app today unless a developer or tool sends an invalid model name.
